- ρ(p²) ≤ pρ(p) and ρ(p) ≤ d for p∉P_0, so ρ(p²)=ρ(p) is not assumed.
- The bound ρ(e) ≤ C_P d^{ω(e)} b.
- The tail and short-sum estimates (8.6)/(8.7).
- The Euler product (8.8) equals ∏σ_p/A_h.
- |σ_p−1| ≤ (3+2d)/p².

No gap found.
toolu_019SdgW5pwr9ixmAHEjdZpBo.numerics_checks:
Computation path:
- reproduce.py checks the SHA-256 of compute.py and counts.cpp against accepted.json; I confirmed the hashes 0f8d7bc6… and 4c4bfa95….
- It re-runs the snapshot code unchanged, including the clang++ recompile, then compares the new output with the archive.
- reproduce.log records 270 rows (90 per polynomial), identical integer counts, max relative V difference 0, identical fits and envelopes.
- I verified independently that generated/snapshot_rerun_results.json equals the archived results.json apart from runtime fields.
- All table and plot fragments for fits, normalised values and sensitivity are read from the re-run output, not the archive.
- build-inputs.json artifact hashes match the shipped generated files, and the PDF hash matches. I could not identify what its 'accepted_snapshot' hash (a5a32517…) refers to; it is not the hash of accepted.json.

Independent checks of my own:
- **Euler products to p ≤ 2·10^6:** C_{k²+1}=0.1380826, C_{k³+2}=0.1356075, C_{2k+1}=0.1426133, formal f=t 0.1284787, Vaughan c_2 0.1284787. All consistent with Table 1's columns at 10^6 and 10^7 and inside its intervals.
- **ρ formulas:** spot-checked by brute force mod p and p².
- **Tail bound:** the bound K/(1−K/N²)·8(N^{-2}+1/(30N)) and its justification are correct.
- **Brute-force V:** a direct residue-class computation of V_f at x=250000 for r=0.01 and 0.1, for all three polynomials (six rows), matches archived V to ≤2e−16 relative.
- **Table 2:** checked against the archived normalised values.
- **Text claims:** −2.61%, +0.53% and −0.65% match Table 3; x^{-2/9}≈0.0135; δ ≤ log10/log x ≈ 0.12; x^{-1/3}r^{-3/2} ≈ 1.6 and 1.6e−3.

Code review of the MT implementation:
- The closed forms A_0Σ_{(t,q)=1}η = (6/π²)∏_{p|q}(p²−2)/(p²−1) and A_0Ση/t² = (36/π⁴)∏p²(p²−2)/(p²−1)² are correct.
- The t_0>√Z_1 tail is handled exactly through B(u)=u−u², and the head/tail split is correct.
- The self-test's g formula is valid for all residues l, not only squarefree ones, so the 4.8e−10 identity check is a genuine test of MT. It covers only x=3000 and q≤40.

Limitations:
- I did not re-run reproduce.py myself: it takes about 12 minutes, needs 5 GB, and would overwrite manuscript/generated.
- I relied on the shipped log for the full-grid equality, plus my own spot checks.
- The exact-shape rows (Table 5) were not recomputed independently beyond the code review.
- The extrapolation envelopes are heuristic, as the text says.

The mathematics is faithful to the archive. Theorem 1.1 (i)–(iii) has exactly P9's hypotheses, error terms, range x^{7/9+δ} ≤ f(y) ≤ x^{1−δ} and η = min(δ/12, 1/(6d)). The weight f'(k) and the class of f are unchanged. I re-derived every merged argument, and I checked each listed correction directly; each one is valid and changes no statement. I found no gap in the archived proofs, so this is not a source-gap case.

The numerics are genuinely recomputed, not copied. The re-run results.json matches the archived file exactly apart from runtime fields. My own independent computation of the C_f values and of Vaughan's c_2 agrees with Table 1. I also brute-forced six rows at x = 250000 for all three polynomials, and they match the archived V exactly.

The verdict is revise for these fixable problems:
- **PDF links:** 125 duplicate hyperref destinations, so many internal links jump to the wrong target.
- **Undocumented statement changes:** a few stated results are slightly strengthened, but changes.md says no statement was changed.
- **Inconsistencies:** some runtime figures and code comments do not match the manuscript.

issues: Layout/navigation (main.tex preamble; main.log lines ~1095–1310): the build produces 125 pdfTeX warnings 'destination with the same identifier (name{equation.N}) has been already used, duplicate ignored' (equation.1–equation.10, lemma.2–lemma.5, remark.2, remark.3, proposition.1x). The hyperref anchor names for equations and theorem-like environments are not section-qualified, so only the first anchor of each name survives. Links such as \eqref{eq:euler} (2.1), (2.2), (8.x) and \cref to Lemma 2.2 / 8.2 etc. therefore jump to the wrong place in the PDF. Fix: make the anchor names section-aware, e.g. \renewcommand{\theHequation}{\thesection.\arabic{equation}} and similar for the theorem counters, or move the numbering setup so hyperref picks it up. Then rebuild and confirm there are no duplicate-destination warnings.

changes.md §4 header and intro ('none of which changes a statement'): several stated results are slightly stronger or more explicit than the archived statements, and none of this is recorded. (a) Proposition 6.2 is stated 'for all real x>0 and all q∈N'; archived P6 states x≥1, 1≤q≤x. This is supported by P6 proof Step 2, 'No use was made of q≤x or x≥1 … holds for all x>0, q≥1'.
